mainTopic: The water for ניסוך המים (the unconsecrated barrel, and why exposed water cannot be strained), the end of פרק לולב וערבה, and the opening משנה of פרק החליל
overview: This amud finishes פרק לולב וערבה and opens פרק החליל. First the גמרא explains why the water for ניסוך המים is kept overnight in a barrel that is not consecrated. One reason is that a consecrated barrel would make the water holy, and then staying overnight (לינה) would disqualify it. חזקיה says a כלי שרת consecrates only with intent, so the rule is a rabbinic decree (גזירה) to stop people from thinking holy water can stay overnight. רבי ינאי, quoting רבי זירא, adds that the decree is needed even if the libation water has a fixed measure, because people might think the barrel was filled for קידוש ידים ורגלים. Next the גמרא asks why water left uncovered (גילוי) cannot simply be strained. It first suggests the משנה disagrees with רבי נחמיה, who holds that a strainer catches snake venom. It then answers that רבי נחמיה allowed this only for ordinary drinking, not for the מזבח, citing the פסוק in מלאכי, 'present it to your governor.' After the הדרן, the new משנה teaches that the flute of the בית השואבה was played five or six days, because it does not override שבת or יום טוב.

steps.title: A consecrated barrel would ruin the water overnight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining why the barrel must be unconsecrated: a consecrated barrel would make the water holy, and holy things left overnight become פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he brought the water in a consecrated barrel, the water would become disqualified by staying overnight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer it was giving to the question of why the משנה says the barrel is not consecrated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כלי שרת makes whatever is placed inside it holy. Once the water is holy, leaving it overnight (לינה) disqualifies it, just like a קרבן left overnight. So the water must sit in a plain barrel until the morning pouring. This explanation assumes the vessel makes the water holy automatically.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated, meaning a vessel that has become a כלי שרת
They become disqualified (פסול)
Remaining overnight, which disqualifies holy items

phrases.english: And if he brings it in a consecrated barrel,
phrases.notes: Refers to the barrel the water is kept in overnight.

phrases.english: they would become disqualified by remaining overnight.
phrases.notes: Holy items left overnight become פסול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes reasoning begun earlier about why the barrel is unconsecrated.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the משנה's requirement through the rule of לינה
steps.terutzMaskana: A consecrated barrel would sanctify the water, and the water would then be disqualified by staying overnight.

steps.title: חזקיה: vessels consecrate only with intent, so it is a rabbinic decree
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה says a כלי שרת only consecrates when there is intent. The real reason for the plain barrel is a גזירה, so people will not think the water was deliberately consecrated and still used after a night.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: Temple vessels only consecrate with intent. The reason is a decree, so that people will not say the water was consecrated on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה gives a different explanation. He holds that the barrel would not automatically make the water holy, so the rule must be a rabbinic decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to חזקיה, one could in theory use a consecrated barrel and simply not intend to consecrate the water. But onlookers would not know that. They might think the water was deliberately made holy and still poured after a night, and conclude that לינה does not disqualify. So the חכמים required a plain barrel.

keyTerms.meaning: Temple service vessels
With intent or awareness
A rabbinic decree made to prevent a mistake
Lest people say (and draw a wrong conclusion)

phrases.english: Chizkiya said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת אֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין אֶלָּא מִדַּעַת,
phrases.english: Temple vessels consecrate only with intent,
phrases.notes: Without intent, the barrel would not make the water holy.

phrases.english: and it is a decree, lest people say

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframes the rule as a rabbinic decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The barrel would automatically make the water holy.
steps.terutzMaskana: Vessels consecrate only with intent. The plain barrel is required by a גזירה to prevent a mistaken conclusion about לינה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It introduces the principle that כלי שרת consecrate only with intent, which the next opinion also accepts.

steps.title: רבי זירא: even granting a measure for the water, a decree is needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי, quoting רבי זירא, says that even if the water has a fixed measure and vessels consecrate only with intent, there is a גזירה: people might think the barrel was filled for washing the כהנים' hands and feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said in the name of רבי זירא: Even if you say the water has a fixed measure, and Temple vessels consecrate only with intent, there is a decree, lest people say the barrel was filled for washing hands and feet.
steps.whatsHappening: A third explanation is given. It describes a different mistake the onlookers might make.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the libation water has a fixed amount (three לוגין), you might think a full barrel cannot be intended for the libation, so nobody would be misled. רבי זירא answers that people might think the barrel was meant for קידוש ידים ורגלים, which has no measure. They would assume it was consecrated for that purpose, then see it poured in the morning and conclude that לינה does not disqualify. So the decree is still needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed, required amount
The כהנים' washing of hands and feet before the עבודה
They filled them

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said that Rabbi Zeira said:
Even if you say there is a fixed measure for the water,
phrases.notes: For the libation, only a set amount is consecrated.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts חזקיה's intent principle but shows the decree is needed even if the water has a measure.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a different mistaken assumption that the decree prevents
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With a fixed measure for the libation, nobody would think a full barrel was consecrated, so no decree is needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: People might think the barrel was consecrated for washing, which has no measure. So the decree still applies.
steps.whatToRemember: Three explanations for the plain barrel: (1) a consecrated barrel would sanctify the water, and לינה would disqualify it; (2) חזקיה: vessels consecrate only with intent, and the rule is a גזירה; (3) רבי זירא: even with a measure for the water, people might think it was filled for קידוש ידים ורגלים.

steps.title: Why not strain the exposed water?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that spilled or uncovered water is disqualified, then asks why the uncovered water cannot simply be passed through a strainer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if it spilled or was left uncovered, and so on. Why should it be disqualified? Let him pass it through a strainer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and challenges it. If the problem is snake venom, why not strain the water?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Uncovered water (גילוי) is forbidden because a snake may have released venom into it. If straining removes that danger, the water should be fixable, and refilling from the כיור should be unnecessary. The challenge assumes straining works.

keyTerms.meaning: It spilled
It was left uncovered (exposed)
But why?
A strainer or filter

phrases.english: If it spilled or was exposed, etc.
But why?
Let him pass it through a strainer.
phrases.notes: This would supposedly remove any venom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that exposed water is disqualified
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If straining removes the danger of venom, the exposed water could be fixed rather than disqualified.
steps.confusionAlert: גילוי here is not about טומאה. It is about the danger that a snake drank from the water and left venom in it.

steps.title: Perhaps the משנה disagrees with רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה does not follow רבי נחמיה. A ברייתא shows that רבי נחמיה holds a strainer protects against venom when the lower vessel is covered, because venom floats and stays on top.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say our משנה does not follow רבי נחמיה? For it was taught: a strainer is subject to the rule of exposure. רבי נחמיה said: When is that? When the lower vessel is uncovered. But when the lower vessel is covered, even if the upper one is uncovered, it is not subject to exposure, because snake venom is like a sponge: it floats and stays in place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes that the משנה follows the תנא קמא and not רבי נחמיה, since רבי נחמיה would allow straining.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא of the ברייתא says a strainer does not help. רבי נחמיה says that if the vessel collecting the filtered water is covered, the venom stays caught in the strainer, because it floats like a sponge. So according to רבי נחמיה straining should work, and the משנה would seem to reject his view. A suggestion that a משנה disagrees with a known תנא is a problem the גמרא will try to avoid.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a tentative suggestion)
Exposure, meaning liquid left uncovered
The lower vessel that receives the strained liquid
The upper vessel or strainer
Snake venom

phrases.english: Shall we say our משנה is not in accordance with Rabbi Nechemya?
As it was taught in a ברייתא:
A strainer is subject to the rule of exposure.
phrases.notes: The view of the תנא קמא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya said: When is this so?
When the lower vessel is exposed,
but when the lower vessel is covered,

because snake venom is like a sponge:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the challenge by suggesting the משנה rejects the view that straining works.
steps.kashyaTarget: Whether the משנה can fit the view of רבי נחמיה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי נחמיה holds that straining removes venom, yet the משנה disqualifies exposed water without allowing straining. So the משנה seems to oppose him.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה allowed straining only for ordinary use
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion: the משנה can follow רבי נחמיה, because he permitted strained water only for an ordinary person, not for an offering to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows רבי נחמיה. Say that רבי נחמיה said this for an ordinary person. But did he say it for the Most High?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה does not contradict רבי נחמיה. His leniency applies to everyday drinking, not to the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strained water may be safe to drink, but it is not of the high quality fitting for the עבודה. So רבי נחמיה would agree that exposed water cannot be used for the ניסוך even after straining. The two sources deal with different settings, so there is no disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (introduces a defense)
An ordinary person, meaning everyday use
The Most High, meaning use for ה׳ and the מזבח

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabbi Nechemya;
say that Rabbi Nechemya said this for an ordinary person,
but did he say it for the Most High?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: he certainly did not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion that the משנה opposes רבי נחמיה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the משנה disagrees with רבי נחמיה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion assumed רבי נחמיה's leniency for drinking also applies to offerings. In fact it is limited to ordinary use.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying strained water stops counting as water or stops being safe. It is safe to drink, but it is not fitting for the מזבח.

steps.title: Support from מלאכי: offer ה׳ only what is fit for a governor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the distinction with the פסוק in מלאכי: you should not offer ה׳ what you would not present to a human governor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי נחמיה not accept the verse: 'Present it now to your governor; will he be pleased with you, or will he show you favor? says ה׳ of hosts'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer with a verse that everyone, including רבי נחמיה, must accept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the נביא rebukes those who bring flawed offerings, asking whether they would dare give such a thing to a governor. Water that was exposed and then strained is not something you would serve an important person. So it is surely unfit for the מזבח, even according to רבי נחמיה.

keyTerms.meaning: And does he not hold...? (rhetorical: surely he does)
Present it now to your governor (מלאכי א:ח)
A governor or important official

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Nechemya not hold:
"Present it now to your governor;
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from מלאכי א:ח.

phrases.english: will he be pleased with you, or will he show you favor,
says ה׳ of hosts"?!
phrases.notes: Rhetorical: of course רבי נחמיה accepts this verse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the distinction between ordinary use and use for the מזבח.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי נחמיה's leniency on strained water does not apply to offerings
steps.whatToRemember: Exposed water cannot be strained for the ניסוך. Even רבי נחמיה, who lets strained water be drunk, agrees that something unfit to serve a governor cannot be offered to ה׳.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a general principle for the עבודה: offerings must meet a standard of honor higher than what is merely permitted for ordinary use.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק לולב וערבה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא formally ends the fourth chapter, פרק לולב וערבה, with the traditional הדרן formula.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק לולב וערבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The chapter about the לולב and ערבה is over. This line is a closing sign-off, not a new argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional farewell that ends every chapter. It expresses love for the תורה we just learned and a promise to come back and review it. No new הלכה is taught here.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (the closing formula said at the end of a chapter)
The name of the fourth chapter of מסכת סוכה, taken from its opening words

steps.whatToRemember: פרק לולב וערבה is finished. Everything after this line belongs to a new chapter with a new topic.

phrases.english: We will return to you, Lulav and Aravah
phrases.notes: This is the line said whenever you finish a chapter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the chapter whose final discussion (Steps 1-7, about the water for the ניסוך and the strainer) has now finished.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The fourth chapter of מסכת סוכה is complete.

steps.title: The flute of the water-drawing celebration is played five or six days
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens פרק החליל. It teaches that the flute of the בית השואבה celebration was played for five or six days of סוכות, because its playing does not override שבת or יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The flute is played for five or six days. This is the flute of the בית השואבה, whose playing does not push aside שבת or יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a new משנה. It tells us how many days the flute was played in the בית המקדש on סוכות, and why the number changes from year to year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סוכות in the בית המקדש lasts seven days, but the flute is never played on שבת or on the first day, which is יום טוב. If the first day falls on שבת, only one day is lost, so the flute plays for six days. If the first day falls on a weekday, then both that יום טוב and the שבת during חול המועד are lost, so the flute plays for only five days.

keyTerms.meaning: The flute; also the name of this new chapter
The place or celebration of the water-drawing, the joyous event connected to drawing water for the ניסוך המים
Overrides, pushes aside (a prohibition such as שבת)
The festival day itself, here the first day of סוכות

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think 'five or six' is a disagreement between two opinions. It is one rule, and the number depends on what day of the week סוכות starts on that year.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that the flute does not override שבת or יום טוב sets up the coming גמרא, which will ask whether this music counts as part of the קרבן service. If it did, it might be allowed to override שבת.

phrases.english: The flute — five and six [days].
phrases.notes: Meaning five days in some years and six in others, depending on when שבת falls.

phrases.english: This is the flute of the Place of the Water-Drawing,
phrases.notes: This tells us which flute: the one played at the שמחת בית השואבה.

phrases.english: which does not override Shabbat
phrases.notes: Playing an instrument is normally forbidden on שבת, and this flute does not push that rule aside.

phrases.english: nor the festival day.
phrases.notes: So it is also not played on the first day of סוכות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the הדרן in Step 8. It is independent of the previous chapter's discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The flute of the בית השואבה is played on סוכות for five or six days, because its playing overrides neither שבת nor יום טוב.
